name: Example Recon Lab
description: A small example lab that shows the authoring format Secure Stack expects.
learning_objectives: Confirm the attacker can reach the target.
Identify the exposed service on the target.
Capture evidence that supports a basic recon finding.
pre_lab_context: This example lab teaches the learner to move from basic connectivity into service validation while paying attention to what each observation actually proves.
environment_overview: The attacker container provides basic recon tools, the target exposes one web application, and the final validation step moves into the browser through the forwarded lab URL.
reflection_prompt: Which observation most clearly confirmed the target's identity before the browser step, and why?
lab_takeaways: Reachability validation gives later recon results a trustworthy baseline.
Enumeration identifies which exposed service deserves deeper investigation.
Application evidence is strongest when you can describe both the service metadata and the visible response.
prerequisites: Familiarity with ICMP, TCP ports, and HTTP
success_criteria: The learner confirms reachability from the attacker shell.
The learner identifies the target's exposed web service.

topology.summary: An attacker shell investigates one exposed web target on an isolated lab network.

nodes.label: Attacker shell
nodes.details: Run recon commands and collect evidence here.

nodes.label: Web target
nodes.details: Hosts the application you are validating.

tasks.title: Verify connectivity
tasks.objective: Confirm the attacker shell can resolve and reach the target host.
tasks.instruction: Confirm the attacker can reach the target host.
tasks.explanation: Connectivity validation proves the isolated lab network is working before you spend time on deeper enumeration.
tasks.why_observation_matters: These signals prove the attacker can trust later failures as service or application issues instead of a broken network path.
tasks.learning_takeaway: This proved the attacker could reach the target before you moved on to deeper recon.
tasks.expected_outcome: You should see successful replies and zero packet loss.
hints: Use the target hostname instead of guessing an IP address.
tasks.remediation_text: If ping fails, confirm the environment launched and the target alias is resolvable.

tasks.title: Identify the exposed service
tasks.objective: Discover the exposed service and capture report-ready evidence.
tasks.instruction: Scan the target to identify open ports and services.
tasks.explanation: Enumeration turns basic reachability into actionable evidence about the attack surface.
tasks.why_observation_matters: These observations tell the learner what is actually exposed and worth investigating further.
tasks.learning_takeaway: This step changed a live host into a mapped service with evidence you can report on.
tasks.expected_outcome: The scan should reveal the open service and enough detail to justify deeper validation.
hints: Use version detection so the output is useful later in the report.

tasks.title: Open the application
tasks.objective: Confirm the service is reachable through the forwarded browser URL.
tasks.instruction: Open the target in your browser.
tasks.explanation: This step links command-line evidence to the learner's actual browser experience.
what_to_observe: Any browser-visible sign that matches the earlier command evidence
tasks.why_observation_matters: This closes the loop between what the tools reported and what a user would actually reach in the browser.
tasks.learning_takeaway: This confirmed that the same service you validated in the shell was also reachable through the forwarded browser URL.
tasks.expected_outcome: The application loads in the browser.
hints: Use the URL returned by the lab launcher instead of guessing the host port.
